title: Background on school marching band
subject: listening

paragraphs.text: SECTION 3
LIZZIE: So how are you getting on with your teaching practice at the High School, Joe?
JOE: Well l've been put in charge of the school marching band, and it's quite a responsibility. l'd like to talk it over with you.
LIZZIE: Go ahead. You'd better start by giving me a bit of background.

JOE: OK. Well the band has students in it from all years, so they're aged 11 to 18, and there are about 50 of them altogether. lt's quite a popular activity within the school. l've never worked with a band of more than 20 before, and this is very different.
LIZZIE: I can imagine.

JOE: They aren't really good enough to enter national band competitions, but they're in a regional one later in the term. Even if they don't win, and I don't expect them to, hopefully it'll be an incentive for them to try and improve.
LIZZIE: Yes, hopefully.

JOE: Well, now the town council's organising a carnival in the summer, and the band has been asked to perform. If you ask me, they aren't really up to it yet, and I need to get them functioning better as a band, and in a very short time.
LIZZIE: Have you been doing anything with them? Apart from practising the music, I mean.

JOE: I played a recording I came across, of a drummer talking about how playing in a band had changed his life. I think it was an aner-ainner speech. I thought it was pretty inspiring, because being in the band had stopped him from getting involved in crime. The students seemed to find it interesting, too.
LIZZIE: That's good.
JOE: l'm planning to show them that old film from the 1940s Strike Up the Band', and talk about it with the students. What do you think?
LIZZIE: Good idea. As it's about a school band, it might make the students realise how much they can achieve if they work together.

JOE: That's what l've got in mind. I'm hoping I can take some of the band to a parade that's going to take place next month. A couple of marching bands will be performing, and the atmosphere should be quite exciting. It depends on whether I can persuade the school to hire a coach or two to take us there.
LIZZIE: Mmm. They sound like good ideas to me.
JOE: Thanks.
JOE: Can I tell you about a few people in the band who l'm finding it quite difficult to cope with? l'm sure you'll have some ideas about what I can do.
LIZZIE: Go ahead.

JOE: There's a flautist who says she loves playing in the band. We rehearse twice a week after school, but she's hardly ever there. Then she looks for me the next day and gives me a very plausible reason - she says she had to help her mother, or she's been ill, but to be honest, I don't believe her.
LIZZIE: Oh dear! Any more students with difficulties?

JOE: Plenty! There's a trumpeter who thinks she's the best musician in the band, though she certainly isn't. She's always saying what she thinks other people should do, which makes my job pretty difficult.
LIZZIE: She sounds a bit of a nightmare!

JOE: You can say that again. One of the trombonists has got an impressive sense of rhythm, and could be an excellent musician - except that he has breathing difficulties, and he doesn't really have enough breath for the trombone. He'd be much better off playing percussion, for instance, but he refuses to give up. So he ends up only playing half the notes.
LIZZIE: I suppose you have to admire his determination.

JOE: Maybe. One of the percussionists isn't too bad, but he never seems to interact with other people, and he always rushes off as soon as the rehearsal ends. I don't know if there are family reasons, or what. But it isn't good in a band, where people really need to feel they're part of a group.
LIZZIE: Hmm.
JOE: There are others too, but at least that gives you an idea of what l'm up against. Do you have any thoughts about what I can do, Lizzie?
莉齐：乔，你在高中的教学实践怎么样了？
乔：嗯，我已经负责学校的军乐队了，这是一个十分重要的任务。我想和你聊一聊这件事。
莉齐：说吧。不过你最好先给我讲一些背景知识。
乔：好的。乐队里面包括了所有年龄的学生，他们的年龄在11到18岁之间，总共有50个人左右。这是学校里非常受欢迎的活动。我以前从未和超过20个人的乐队合作过，所以这很特别。
莉齐：我可以想象得到。
乔：他们还没有足够的能力进入全国乐队比赛，但是他们在这个学期后期会进入区域性比赛。 即使他们没有获胜，我也没指望他们能获胜，只是希望这会激励他们努力并且进步。
莉齐：是的，希望如此。
乔：嗯，现在小镇委员会要在夏天组织一个狂欢节，他们已经请了我们乐队去演出。硬要我说的话，其实他们还没有达到那个水平，我需要让他们在很短的时间内作为一个乐队整体表现得更好。
莉齐：你有没有和他们一起做过什么？我的意思是，除了练习音乐之外。
乔：我放了一个我偶然发现的录像，一位鼓手谈论参加乐队如何改变了他的生活。这好像是一个餐后演讲。我觉得这很鼓舞人心，因为参加乐队使他没有他卷入犯罪。学生似乎也觉得它很有趣。
莉齐：这很不错。
乔：我打算给学生们放这个40年代的老电影“Strike Up the Band”，并与他们讨论。你觉得怎么样？
莉齐：好主意。因为它是关于一个学校乐队，它可能会让学生意识到如果他们齐心协力，他们可以做的多好。
乔：这就是我所想的。我希望我能把乐队中的一些人带到下个月即将举行的游行中。几个游行乐队将会表演，气氛应该会非常令人兴奋。这取决于我是否可以说服学校聘请一两位教练带我们去。
莉齐：嗯。我觉得听起来很不错。
乔：谢谢。
乔：我可以告诉你，我发现乐队里的一些人很难应付吗？我相信你会对于我能做什么提些建议。
莉齐：说吧。
乔：有一个吹长笛的学生说她非常喜欢在乐队里演奏。我们放学后每周排练两次，但她几乎没来过。然后她会在第二天找我，并给我一个可信的理由——她说她必须帮助她的母亲，或者她病了，但说实话，我不相信她。
莉齐：哦，亲爱的！还有其他遇到困难的学生吗？
乔：太多了！有一个小号手认为她是乐队中最好的音乐家，尽管很显然她不是。她总是说她认为其他人应该做什么，这使我的工作变得非常困难。
莉齐：她听起来有点难以对付！
乔：你可以再感叹一次了。有一个长号手有一种令人敬佩的的节奏感，并且可能是一位出色的音乐家——除了他有呼吸困难，而且他的长号也没有足够的气息。如果他打击打击乐会好得多，但他拒绝放弃。所以他最终只吹演奏了一半的音符。
莉齐：我想你必须佩服他的决心。
乔：也许吧。有一个打击乐手问题并不是太糟糕，但他似乎永远不会与其他人互动，而且他总是在排练结束后立即赶走。 我不知道是否有家庭原因，或者是什么。但是在一个乐队中并不好，人们真的需要觉得自己是这个团队的一部分。
莉齐：嗯。
乔：其实还有其他人，但至少可以让你了解我在面对什么。莉齐，你对我能做些什么有什么建议吗？

Question 27-30

What problem does Joe mention in connection with each of the following band members?

Choose the correct answer and move it into the gap.

questions.explanation:
27~30题为搭配题，难度略高。

27.题干词flautist原词重现，帮助定位。选项D. missed too many rehearsals在原文中被同义替换为but she's hardly ever there，意思是她几乎不怎么参加彩排，也就是很多场彩排未能出现。

28.题干词trumpeter原词重现。选项B. keeps making unhelpful suggestions在原文中被解释性同义替换为she's always saying what she thinks other people should do, which makes my job pretty difficult，她总是会提出一些她认为其他人需要做的事，使得我的工作很难开展，表示她总是提出些无用的建议。

29.题干词trombonist原词重现，帮助定位。选项E. has a health problem被原文he has breathing difficulties and he doesn't really have enough breath for the trombone同义替换，意思是他在呼吸方面有一些问题，吹长号时气息常常不足，也就表示他有健康方面的问题。

30.题干词percussionist原词重现，帮助定位。选项F. doesn't mix with other students，与其他学生合不来，在原文中被同义替换为he never seems to interact with other people, and he always rushes off as soon as the rehearsal ends。该句意为：他看起来从不跟其他人互动，排练一结束就赶紧溜了。表示他不愿意跟他人交流，不合群。

SECTION 3

LIZZIE: So how are you getting on with your teaching practice at the High School, Joe?

JOE: Well l've been put in charge of the school marching band, and it's quite a responsibility. l'd like to talk it over with you.

LIZZIE: Go ahead. You'd better start by giving me a bit of background.

JOE: OK. Well the band has students in it from all years, so they're aged 11 to 18, and there are about 50 of them altogether. lt's quite a popular activity within the school. l've never worked with a band of more than 20 before, and this is very different.

LIZZIE: I can imagine.

JOE: They aren't really good enough to enter national band competitions, but they're in a regional one later in the term. Even if they don't win, and I don't expect them to, hopefully it'll be an incentive for them to try and improve.

LIZZIE: Yes, hopefully.

JOE: Well, now the town council's organising a carnival in the summer, and the band has been asked to perform. If you ask me, they aren't really up to it yet, and I need to get them functioning better as a band, and in a very short time.

LIZZIE: Have you been doing anything with them? Apart from practising the music, I mean.

JOE: I played a recording I came across, of a drummer talking about how playing in a band had changed his life. I think it was an aner-ainner speech. I thought it was pretty inspiring, because being in the band had stopped him from getting involved in crime. The students seemed to find it interesting, too.

LIZZIE: That's good.

JOE: l'm planning to show them that old film from the 1940s Strike Up the Band', and talk about it with the students. What do you think?

LIZZIE: Good idea. As it's about a school band, it might make the students realise how much they can achieve if they work together.

JOE: That's what l've got in mind. I'm hoping I can take some of the band to a parade that's going to take place next month. A couple of marching bands will be performing, and the atmosphere should be quite exciting. It depends on whether I can persuade the school to hire a coach or two to take us there.

LIZZIE: Mmm. They sound like good ideas to me.

JOE: Thanks.

 

JOE: Can I tell you about a few people in the band who l'm finding it quite difficult to cope with? l'm sure you'll have some ideas about what I can do.

LIZZIE: Go ahead.

JOE: There's a flautist who says she loves playing in the band. We rehearse twice a week after school, but she's hardly ever there. Then she looks for me the next day and gives me a very plausible reason - she says she had to help her mother, or she's been ill, but to be honest, I don't believe her.

LIZZIE: Oh dear! Any more students with difficulties?

JOE: Plenty! There's a trumpeter who thinks she's the best musician in the band, though she certainly isn't. She's always saying what she thinks other people should do, which makes my job pretty difficult.

LIZZIE: She sounds a bit of a nightmare!

JOE: You can say that again. One of the trombonists has got an impressive sense of rhythm, and could be an excellent musician - except that he has breathing difficulties, and he doesn't really have enough breath for the trombone. He'd be much better off playing percussion, for instance, but he refuses to give up. So he ends up only playing half the notes.

LIZZIE: I suppose you have to admire his determination.

JOE: Maybe. One of the percussionists isn't too bad, but he never seems to interact with other people, and he always rushes off as soon as the rehearsal ends. I don't know if there are family reasons, or what. But it isn't good in a band, where people really need to feel they're part of a group.

LIZZIE: Hmm.

JOE: There are others too, but at least that gives you an idea of what l'm up against. Do you have any thoughts about what I can do, Lizzie?

 

莉齐：乔，你在高中的教学实践怎么样了？

乔：嗯，我已经负责学校的军乐队了，这是一个十分重要的任务。我想和你聊一聊这件事。

莉齐：说吧。不过你最好先给我讲一些背景知识。

乔：好的。乐队里面包括了所有年龄的学生，他们的年龄在11到18岁之间，总共有50个人左右。这是学校里非常受欢迎的活动。我以前从未和超过20个人的乐队合作过，所以这很特别。

莉齐：我可以想象得到。

乔：他们还没有足够的能力进入全国乐队比赛，但是他们在这个学期后期会进入区域性比赛。 即使他们没有获胜，我也没指望他们能获胜，只是希望这会激励他们努力并且进步。

莉齐：是的，希望如此。

乔：嗯，现在小镇委员会要在夏天组织一个狂欢节，他们已经请了我们乐队去演出。硬要我说的话，其实他们还没有达到那个水平，我需要让他们在很短的时间内作为一个乐队整体表现得更好。

莉齐：你有没有和他们一起做过什么？我的意思是，除了练习音乐之外。

乔：我放了一个我偶然发现的录像，一位鼓手谈论参加乐队如何改变了他的生活。这好像是一个餐后演讲。我觉得这很鼓舞人心，因为参加乐队使他没有他卷入犯罪。学生似乎也觉得它很有趣。

莉齐：这很不错。

乔：我打算给学生们放这个40年代的老电影“Strike Up the Band”，并与他们讨论。你觉得怎么样？

莉齐：好主意。因为它是关于一个学校乐队，它可能会让学生意识到如果他们齐心协力，他们可以做的多好。

乔：这就是我所想的。我希望我能把乐队中的一些人带到下个月即将举行的游行中。几个游行乐队将会表演，气氛应该会非常令人兴奋。这取决于我是否可以说服学校聘请一两位教练带我们去。

莉齐：嗯。我觉得听起来很不错。

乔：谢谢。

 

乔：我可以告诉你，我发现乐队里的一些人很难应付吗？我相信你会对于我能做什么提些建议。

莉齐：说吧。

乔：有一个吹长笛的学生说她非常喜欢在乐队里演奏。我们放学后每周排练两次，但她几乎没来过。然后她会在第二天找我，并给我一个可信的理由——她说她必须帮助她的母亲，或者她病了，但说实话，我不相信她。

莉齐：哦，亲爱的！还有其他遇到困难的学生吗？

乔：太多了！有一个小号手认为她是乐队中最好的音乐家，尽管很显然她不是。她总是说她认为其他人应该做什么，这使我的工作变得非常困难。

莉齐：她听起来有点难以对付！

乔：你可以再感叹一次了。有一个长号手有一种令人敬佩的的节奏感，并且可能是一位出色的音乐家——除了他有呼吸困难，而且他的长号也没有足够的气息。如果他打击打击乐会好得多，但他拒绝放弃。所以他最终只吹演奏了一半的音符。

莉齐：我想你必须佩服他的决心。

乔：也许吧。有一个打击乐手问题并不是太糟糕，但他似乎永远不会与其他人互动，而且他总是在排练结束后立即赶走。 我不知道是否有家庭原因，或者是什么。但是在一个乐队中并不好，人们真的需要觉得自己是这个团队的一部分。

莉齐：嗯。

乔：其实还有其他人，但至少可以让你了解我在面对什么。莉齐，你对我能做些什么有什么建议吗？
